headline: Google 发 Gemini 4，GPT-6.1 Sol 需求爆表，agent 协作成热议
bullets: Google 发布 Gemini 4（代号 Argon），builder 们普遍叫好；但认为 Google 在编程工具 Antigravity 和个人 agent Spark 上还得再加把劲。
OpenAI 的 GPT-6.1 Sol 是史上需求最高的模型，API 和订阅两边都超负荷，团队正在紧急扩容。
ChatGPT 现在可以直接构建和部署 MCP servers，还能限制访问权限或公开分享——agent 接外部工具的门槛又降了一截。
多智能体协作成了焦点：Garry Tan 说别的编辑器只能自上而下指挥子 agent，而这里 agent 之间能像同侪一样互相对话、自我协调。
企业侧在谈「AI 部署层」的机会（Levie），Google Labs 的 Opal 并入 Skills，Meta 支持用 Make 一键发布 VR 应用。
sentiment: 整体是「兴奋 + 吐槽」并存：对 Gemini 4 和新 agent 能力普遍叫好，但同时抱怨 CI/GitHub 拖慢开发、agent 互相刷屏太吵，也担心模型产能跟不上。

posts.name: Guillermo Rauch
posts.text:
Most token aggregators have extreme noise from ① token promos from/to providers that train on your data or ② providers that *claim* to be ZDR.

Vercel AI Gateway is the largest trustworthy datasource to understand global AI token flows, because we have real usage, from real customers, an at-scale platform (400k+ paying customers and thousands of enterprises), and zero markup.

Notably… every week we turn down "free token" promos from companies that come to us with dubious claims of Zero Data Retention (ZDR) and questionable reputations. We also don't get a kick out of having the "most providers". Most providers suck. You want the *best* providers.

We put in as much work in engineering our gateway, as in our legal, compliance, privacy, and backoffice operations to responsibly serve trillions of tokens every day. We're here for the long haul.

posts.name: Garry Tan
posts.text:
I asked Secretary Duffy what Americans should be able to do, if we get this decade right, that they can't do today.

Sean Duffy is the Secretary of Transportation, and he sat down with me at our Startup Industrial Base event in DC today. He went straight to how our country's air traffic gets managed.

At the command center, people sit in front of six screens with a paper flight chart above them, trying to make the calls on weather and routing.

His example: four planes reach the same runway at the same time and only one can land. See it two hours out, speed up two, slow one down, and each one lands when the runway is open. "Like, not complicated stuff, but we don't do any of this."

Paper and pencil and minimal human augmentation from software looks like this: Say an airport can take 15 planes in a 15 minute window. "Well, the airlines will schedule 32." He says he's handing the airlines that data and asking them to spread out.

The tool is SMART, from Air Space Intelligence, a small company he says competed with the biggest companies and won. It predicts. His stage example: a 2.5 hour ground stop might only need 45 minutes. He's taken heat for supposedly handing air traffic control to AI. Duffy's answer? "it's dumb AI, not smart AI." Controllers still make every call.

None of this needs a breakthrough. It needs the will of the people to know they need to use software and be ok with AI augmentation instead of insisting on a paper chart and copper wire.
posts.summaryZh: 转述他问美国交通部长 Duffy：如果这个十年走对了，美国人应该能做哪些今天还做不到的事。

If you run a service and want to get in front of 20M+ developers and the billions of agents they'll ship, add yourself to Connect.

posts.name: Aaron Levie
posts.text:
There's a huge opportunity right now in being the deployment layer for AI into the economy. The amount of work it takes to change out workflows in enterprises tends to be far greater than anyone realizes or would prefer. Clearly this is what the applied layer of AI is going to look like in the form of software and agents, but also it opens up new services firms opportunities.

Legacy systems need to be moved to the cloud, data organization and access needs to be updated, software needs to be connected to agents in new ways, workflows need to be reengineered for agents, HITL needs to be figured out for the process, evals need to be generated and maintained, and the entire system needs to be continually updated as new models get released and new capabilities emerge. And the full list may even be longer.

AI is not the same as just deploying software. Software you generally did the implementation of an existing, well understood category of technology, then stepped back and the customer kept running. With AI agents, you're delivering actual work augmentation to the organization, which has a completely different set of complexities associated with it. You're no longer deploying tools that the company is merely enabled by, you're deploying work output in a process. Completely different implementation and enablement process.

As a result, this is going to open up lots of new kinds of firms and plays for existing firms to diffuse AI into organizations. We're going to see approaches by industry, by size of company, and by problem inside of companies. Traditional SIs will modernize and adapt (some will clearly not adapt as well), and new entrants will also be founded in this period that take advantage of this window. Great time to be an FDE or FDE firm.
posts.summaryZh: 认为当前最大的机会是做「AI 落地到经济中的部署层」——企业改工作流的成本远高于换模型本身。

posts.name: Google Labs
posts.text:
💠 Opal shines on in Skills! 💠

When we launched Opal in Google Labs, it was an experiment to learn how you customize your workflows. Your incredible creativity taught us so much — first inspiring Gems made by Labs, and today, supporting the global launch of skills in @GeminiApp! ✨

Skills are a faster way to automate repetitive tasks and save custom instructions right in chat - built from the learnings we had from Opal. As skills roll out globally, we will be saying a bittersweet farewell to Opal. The experiment will be shutting down on Nov 17, 2026.

Whether you built mini-apps on https://t.co/YOHh8P89yg or tried Gems in Gemini, thank you for shaping the future of customizable AI. Opal lives on in every skill you build next. 💙

posts.name: Aditya Agarwal
posts.text:
The question I keep on asking everyone @spc is "What is the maximalist version of this company?".

Perhaps this has always been true....but if you are building a company today, then the only way is to have the boldest, most audacious and maximalist version of the idea and how it can change the arc of the future.

If you start small, you will struggle to get funding, hire great people and ultimately to make a dent in the future.

This is the paradox of AI. It makes building easier but dramatically raises the floor on what it means to be a great startup.

posts.name: Nan Yu
posts.text:
It’s interesting to contrast, what different companies take for granted in their internal cultures

I’ve only been at OpenAI for about a week, and the thing that stands out is absurdly high bias towards action

This shows up in ways big and small…

Sometimes you have a casual discussion about a possible feature, and the PR is sitting in front of you by the time you get back to your desk 

Or you meet someone on Slack and say: “let’s grab lunch next week” and the meeting invites on your calendar within the next five minutes

This has its downsides. because it often feels like everything’s behind a hair trigger, and things just change out from under you— but you can’t really teach this energy, and if you ever lose it, it’s unbelievably hard to get it back

Open AI is not a tiny company anymore. It’s got several massive buildings in San Francisco, it’s impressive that this energy still persists
posts.summaryZh: 刚加入 OpenAI 一周，最让他印象深刻的是内部文化的「高标准」到了荒谬的程度。
